answer: The Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus algorithm can resist fake-identity attacks through its voting mechanism, where agents verify the identity of their peers by checking the digital signature of each proposal. This process creates a digital relic of the agent's previous votes, ensuring that a malicious agent cannot forge a new identity by submitting multiple proposals. As proposals flow into the network like water into an inlet, the BFT algorithm filters out fake votes, preventing a malicious agent from polluting the river of legitimate proposals.
